title: A worker's brief tells it to commit by turn 1 when dispatch's cap is not above the commit margin
goal: worker_rules in bl_dispatch.py gives the brief a commit-by turn of cap minus COMMIT_MARGIN when the cap is above twice the margin and half the cap otherwise (at least 1), so dispatch --max-turns 10 writes 'by turn 5 commit what you have' and --max-turns 100 still writes 'by turn 85'. Found by the SP-mujl7ebh review.

run: import sys;sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import bl_dispatch as d;f=lambda n:" ".join(x for x in d.worker_rules(".","X","work/X",n) if "turn cap" in x);sys.exit(0 if "by turn 5 " in f(10) and "by turn 85 " in f(100) and "by turn 1 " not in f(10) else 1)

notes: Premise (reproduces: the repro, which asserts the turns the goal names): worker_rules clamps the commit-by turn with max(cap - COMMIT_MARGIN, 1), so cap 10 writes by turn 1. Settled in the goal, not a gate: half the cap at or below twice the margin, no dispatch refusal. The code is bl_dispatch.py line 223 (compose_brief and worker_rules callers of commit_by); backlog.md and tools.md name the turn cap rule.
